## Notebook Overview

**Inputs:**

- `../../../data/acs_step2_16.feather` — 2012–2016 ACS tract measures (SCAG region).
- `../../../data/acs_step2_24.feather` — 2020–2024 ACS tract measures (SCAG region), aggregated to 2010 tracts.

**Outputs:**

- `../../../data/acs_full.feather` — the ACS tract panel: 2016 and 2024 measures
  (2016 dollars inflation-adjusted to 2024) side by side on `tr2010_id`, with
  change measures (level `*POST` ratios and share/rate `*PPC` percentage-point
  differences) and their coefficients of variation.

This notebook:

1. Sets up the environment (packages, helper functions, data directory)
2. Imports and prepares the 2020–2024 and 2012–2016 tract measures (rename, select, inflation-adjust)
3. Merges the two surveys and calculates change variables
4. Validates the saved output

This step only **merges** existing tract measures and derives change variables;
both inputs are already restricted to the SCAG region (in `02_assemble.Rmd`), so
no further sample restriction happens here.

# 1. Set up environment

## 1.1 Load packages

```{r load-packages, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
rm(list = ls())

library(here)          # project-root-relative paths via here::here()
library(Hmisc)
library(dplyr)
library(tidycensus)
library(tidyverse)
library(spatstat)
library(matrixStats)
library(survey)
library(srvyr)
```

## 1.2 Load helper functions

This stage's helpers — feather I/O, the survey `merge_df()`, variable
renaming/selection, inflation adjustment, and the change-variable functions —
live in `R/merge_helpers.R`. That file is self-contained for this notebook (its
`merge_df()` differs from the one used by `02_assemble.Rmd`).

```{r load-helpers}
source(here::here("R", "merge_helpers.R"))
```

## 1.3 Set data directory

```{r set-paths}
# Trailing slash is intentional: save_data() builds paths with paste0().
data_dir <- "../../../data/"
```

# 2. Import and prepare survey measures

## 2.1 Load and prepare 2020–2024 measures

Load the assembled 2024 tract measures, suffix their variables with `_24`, and
keep the analytic variable set plus a few extra quality/derived columns
(`pct_miss_rent`, `pct_miss_hval`, `tc_flag_rent_24`, `interp_rent`). The analytic
set now also carries the renamed multifamily count `mf5E`, the non-single-family-
attached count `nsfaE`, and the rental / for-sale vacancy rates
`pctrvacE` / `pctsvacE` (added to `rename_vars()` so they get the year suffix).

```{r prep-24}
# # Load 2005-2009 ACS data
# rent_09 <- load_data(data_dir, NULL, "acs_09_step2.feather")

# Load 2020-2024 ACS data
acs_24 <- load_data(data_dir, NULL, "acs_step2_24.feather")
report_n(acs_24, "2024 tract measures loaded")

# Rename variables
acs_24 <- rename_vars(acs_24, "24")

# Select variables
# var_list <- c("pct_miss_rent", "pct_tc_rent")
# var_list <- c("pct_miss_rent", "pct_miss_hval", "tc_flag_rent_24", "interp_rent", "interp_rentCV", "interp_rentM")
var_list <- c("pct_miss_rent", "pct_miss_hval", "tc_flag_rent_24", "interp_rent")
acs_24 <- select_vars(acs_24, "24", var_list)

# Apply inflation adjustment
# n/a
```

## 2.2 Load and prepare 2012–2016 measures

### Decision: Inflation-adjust 2016 dollars to 2024 dollars

Dollar-denominated 2016 measures (median rent, lower-quartile contract rent,
median household income, median house value — estimates and their margins of
error) are multiplied by **1.307** to express them in 2024 dollars, so that
change variables in §3.2 compare *real* values across the two periods. The
adjustment is applied only to the 2016 vintage (`infl_adj_vars(..., "16")`).

Inflation adjustment uses CPI-U annual averages (BLS, CPI-U, U.S. city average,
all items) to adjust 2016 dollars to 2024 dollars. Factor = 313.689 / 240.007 ≈
1.307.

```{r prep-16}
# Load 2012-2016 ACS data
acs_16 <- load_data(data_dir, NULL, "acs_step2_16.feather")
report_n(acs_16, "2016 tract measures loaded")

# Rename variables
acs_16 <- rename_vars(acs_16, "16")

# Select variables
var_list <- c("m_flag_rent" , "m_flag_lqcrent", "m_flag_rhu", "m_flag_med_hval",
               "zero_flag_rhu", "tc_flag_rent", "tc_flag_lqcrent", "tc_flag_med_hval")
acs_16 <- select_vars(acs_16, "16", var_list)

# Apply inflation adjustmen
summary(acs_16$rentE_16)
acs_16 <- infl_adj_vars(acs_16, "16")
summary(acs_16$rentE_16)

# table(acs_16$m_flag1_16, useNA="ifany")
```

# 3. Merge surveys and calculate change variables

## 3.1 Merge 2016 and 2024 tract measures

### Decision: Keep all tracts (full join, not inner join)

The two surveys are full-joined on `tr2010_id` and **all** tracts are retained —
the inner-join filter (`filter(merge=="both")`) is intentionally left commented
out. Tracts present in only one period keep `NA` for the other period's measures;
change variables (§3.2) are guarded so they are `NA` when a base value is
missing or zero. There is therefore **no row-dropping filter** in this notebook.

```{r merge-surveys}
# Merge post rent data
n_16 <- nrow(acs_16)
n_24 <- nrow(acs_24)
acs_16_24 <- merge_df(acs_16, acs_24)
table(acs_16_24$merge)
cat(sprintf("Merged %s (2016) and %s (2024) tracts -> %s panel rows\n",
            formatC(n_16, format = "d", big.mark = ","),
            formatC(n_24, format = "d", big.mark = ","),
            formatC(nrow(acs_16_24), format = "d", big.mark = ",")))

# Keep all
acs_16_24 <- acs_16_24 |>
  # dplyr::filter(merge=="both") |>
  select(-c(merge)) |>
  mutate(base_id=TRUE)

acs_full <- acs_16_24

# # Merge pre- baseline rent data

# table(rent_full$merge)

# # Keep all

```

## 3.2 Calculate change variables and their CVs

### Decision: Level changes are ratios; share / rate changes are percentage-point differences

Dollar- and count-denominated change ("POST") variables are the ratio of the
2024 value to the (inflation-adjusted) 2016 value, defined only where the 2016
denominator is positive (otherwise `NA`).

Share and rate change variables are instead **percentage-point differences**
(`value_24 - value_16`, named `*PPC`): the renter-occupied share `pctrhuPPC`, the
overall vacant share `pctvacPPC`, and the rental / for-sale vacancy rates
`pctrvacPPC` / `pctsvacPPC`. A difference is the natural change for a rate, is
defined wherever both periods are present (so it avoids the large zero-base `NA`
counts a ratio produces for rates that are often `0`), and is bounded in roughly
[−1, 1]. The carried `mf5E` / `nsfaE` counts are levels only and get no change
variable.

`m_flag_rentPOST` / `m_flag_rhuPOST` mark missing change values. Coefficients of
variation for the key (level) change variables come from ratio-MOE propagation in
`calc_cv_change_vars()`; the share / rate `*PPC` differences carry no CV.

```{r change-vars}
# Calculate change variables
acs_full <- calc_change_vars(acs_full)

table(acs_full$m_flag_rentPOST)
table(acs_full$m_flag_rhuPOST)

# Quick distribution check on the share / rate percentage-point changes
# (expected range roughly [-1, 1])
summary(acs_full$pctrhuPPC)
summary(acs_full$pctvacPPC)
summary(acs_full$pctrvacPPC)
summary(acs_full$pctsvacPPC)

# Calculate CV for change variables
acs_full <- calc_cv_change_vars (acs_full)
```

## 3.3 Save the ACS tract panel

**Output:** `acs_full.feather` — the ACS tract panel feeding the downstream
analysis stages.

```{r save-panel}
report_n(acs_full, "ACS tract panel to save")

# Save file
acs_full %>%
  arrow::write_feather(paste0(data_dir, "acs_full.feather"))
```

## 3.4 Summarize coefficients of variation

Quick reliability check: CV distributions for the level and change measures.

```{r summarize-cv}
print("Summary Stats: CV, 2016 Rental housing units ")
summary(acs_full$rhuCV_16)
print("Summary Stats: CV, 2024 Rental housing units ")
summary(acs_full$rhuCV_24)

print("Summary Stats: CV, 2016 Median rent ")
summary(acs_full$rentCV_16)
print("Summary Stats: CV, 2024 Median rent ")
summary(acs_full$rentCV_24)

print("Summary Stats: CV, Rent change")
summary(acs_full$rentPOSTCV)
print("Summary Stats: CV, Rental housing unit change")
summary(acs_full$rhuPOSTCV)

print("Summary Stats: CV, Rent change")
summary(acs_full$interp_rentPOSTCV)
print("Summary Stats: CV, Rental housing unit change")
summary(acs_full$rhuPOSTCV)


print("Summary Stats: CV, 2016 Median household income ")
summary(acs_full$med_hhincCV_16)
print("Summary Stats: CV, 2024 Median household income ")
summary(acs_full$med_hhincCV_24)

print("Summary Stats: CV, Median income change")
summary(acs_full$med_hhincPOSTCV)

cor(acs_full$interp_rentPOST, acs_full$rentPOST, use = "complete.obs")
# correlation between interpolated rent change and weighed median rent change is .88
```

# 4. Validate outputs

Re-loads the saved panel and checks key uniqueness, missingness on critical
variables, the encoding of the flag columns, and the distribution of every
numeric column.

```{r reload-panel}
acs_out <- arrow::read_feather(paste0(data_dir, "acs_full.feather"))
```

## 4.1 Check key uniqueness and duplicates

Expected: the panel is unique on `tr2010_id`.

```{r validate-keys-panel}
cat("acs_full:", nrow(acs_out), "rows |",
    n_distinct(acs_out$tr2010_id), "unique tr2010_id |",
    sum(duplicated(acs_out$tr2010_id)), "duplicate ids\n")
```

## 4.2 Check missingness on critical variables

Expected: no missing `tr2010_id`. Missingness in the change ratios reflects
tracts present in only one period or with a non-positive base value; we report
counts rather than impose a threshold.

```{r validate-missingness-panel}
cat("acs_full missing tr2010_id:    ", sum(is.na(acs_out$tr2010_id)), "\n")
cat("acs_full missing rentE_16:     ", sum(is.na(acs_out$rentE_16)), "\n")
cat("acs_full missing rentE_24:     ", sum(is.na(acs_out$rentE_24)), "\n")
cat("acs_full missing rentPOST:     ", sum(is.na(acs_out$rentPOST)), "\n")
cat("acs_full missing interp_rentPOST:", sum(is.na(acs_out$interp_rentPOST)), "\n")
```

## 4.3 Check flag-variable encoding

The data-quality / change flags (`m_flag_*`, `zero_flag_*`, `tc_flag_*`) should
be 0/1 integers, not string labels. The `base_id` / `post_id` columns are
join indicators (logical) and are reported for transparency.

```{r validate-flags-panel}
flag_cols <- grep("^(m_flag_|zero_flag_|tc_flag_)", names(acs_out), value = TRUE)
for (f in flag_cols) {
  cat("acs_full", f, "-> class:", class(acs_out[[f]]),
      "| values:", paste(sort(unique(acs_out[[f]])), collapse = ", "), "\n")
}
cat("acs_full base_id class:", class(acs_out$base_id),
    "| post_id class:", class(acs_out$post_id), "\n")
```

## 4.4 Summarize numeric variable distributions

Mean, min, and max for every numeric column in the panel. Watch for impossible
values (negative counts, change ratios far from a plausible range, or shares
outside [0, 1]).

```{r validate-numeric-panel}
print_numeric_summary(acs_out, "acs_full")
```
